Q. 
Please explain how the corrections and updates are organized. 
1 
A. 
The exhibits submitted in this filing show corrections and/or updates and 
2 
indicate the change from the original filing.  The exhibits are labeled with 
3 
“CU” after the original label.  For example, Exhibit __ (RRP-1) in the April 
4 
30 filing is the Statement of Operating Income.  The exhibit showing the 
5 
corrections and/or updates to the Statement of Operating Income is labeled 
6 
Exhibit ___ (RRP-1CU).  The first page of each exhibit provides a summary 
7 
of all adjustments made and reflected in that exhibit.  This summary, or lead 
8 
page, is identified as “Corrections and Updates” under each exhibit number.  
9 
The revised schedules and pages supporting each exhibit correspond to the 
10 
schedules and pages originally filed.  The Company has only included 
11 
exhibits, summaries, schedules, and pages where corrections and/or updates 
12 
were made.   
13 
 
14 
The information requests referenced in the Panel’s testimony are included in 
15 
the workpapers in Exhibit ___ (RRP-11CU) and correspond to the specific 
16 
exhibits and schedules where the corrections and/or updates were made.  For 
17 
example, if a correction and/or update is shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-3CU), 
18 
Schedule 2 based on a response to an information request, that information 
19 
request is included in the workpapers supporting Exhibit ___ (RRP-3CU), 
20 


--- Page 6 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 4 of 24 
 
Schedule 2.  Where the attachments to information requests are voluminous, 
1 
the Company included only the written response and relevant attachments.   
2

VI. 
Federal and State Income Taxes 
9 
Q. 
Has the Company made any corrections or updates to federal and state 
10 
income tax expense? 
11 
A. 
Yes, the Company made adjustments to reflect changes to the amortization of 
12 
excess accumulated deferred income tax (“ADIT”) and to reflect the flow 
13 
through effect of changes in rate base on income tax expense. 
14 
 
15 
Q. 
Please describe the changes to the amortization of excess ADIT. 
16 
A. 
There are two changes effecting the amortization of excess ADIT.  First, the 
17 
overall excess ADIT amount was rolled forward from December 2018 to 
18 
March 2019.  Second the Company changed the amortization life for the 
19 
unprotected, non-plant excess ADIT. 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 19 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 17 of 24 
 
Q. 
Please explain why the Company rolled forward the excess ADIT 
1 
balances to March 2019. 
2 
A. 
The Company rolled the excess ADIT balances forward to match the plant roll 
3 
forward balance and to reflect adjustments to income tax reserves that resulted 
4 
from the settlement of the August 24, 2007 to March 31, 2009 federal income 
5 
tax audit.  For the audit adjustments that were temporary, the current income 
6 
tax was booked at 35 percent, the deferred tax was booked at 21 percent, and 
7 
the difference increased or decreased the regulatory liability for excess ADIT.  
8 
The amortization lives were applied to the adjusted balances, resulting in 
9 
changed total excess ADIT amortization amounts. 
10 
 
11 
Q. 
Were there any other changes related to the amortization of excess 
12 
ADIT? 
13 
A. 
Yes, the Company made adjustments to the amortization period for excess 
14 
ADIT and to reflect shifts between unprotected and protected excess ADIT.  
15 
As KEDLI was an asset purchase, there was a tax basis adjustment in the 
16 
PowerTax system that represented the book depreciation reserve at the time of 
17 
the asset purchase.  Originally, during the implementation of the module, no 
18 
book depreciation was allocated to this purchase accounting adjustment when 
19 
it should have attracted book depreciation.  The allocation of book 
20 
depreciation was corrected in a later version.  This resulted in the protected 
21 


--- Page 20 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 18 of 24 
 
excess ADIT decreasing and the unprotected plant excess ADIT increasing.  
1 
This also resulted in lower annual protected amortization amounts.  These 
2 
adjusted amounts are set forth in Exhibit ___ (RRP-6CU), Workpaper 1 in a 
3 
manner similar to the April 30 filing.  However, using the remaining book life 
4 
of 47 years for unprotected plant amortization life and 14 years for 
5 
unprotected non-plant balances resulted in an annual recovery from customers 
6 
rather than a return of excess ADIT, as would be expected.  To avoid 
7 
collecting from customers only to return the money in a future period, the 
8 
Company proposes to increase the recovery period of unprotected non-plant 
9 
excess ADIT to 25 years to reverse the negative impact. 
10 
 
11

15 
of a lead Corrections and Updates page, a Summary with three pages, and six 
16

17 
assets and liabilities (Schedule 2), federal and state accumulated deferred 
18 
income taxes (Schedule 3), working capital (Schedule 4), and the lead lag 
19 
study (Schedule 5).

A. 
Forecast of Net Utility Plant In Service 
1 
Q. 
Please describe the changes made to the forecast of average net utility 
2 
plant, as shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-7CU), Schedule 1.   
3 
A. 
Schedule 1 reflects three adjustments.  The first adjustment reflects updates to 
4 
the Company’s net utility plant forecast.  The Company updated the forecast 
5 
to use the actual March 31, 2019 construction work in progress, plant in 
6 
service, depreciation reserve, and retirement work in progress beginning 
7 
balances.  The Company also updated the composite depreciation rates using 
8 
depreciable plant balances as of March 2019. 
9 
 
10 
The second adjustment updates the Company’s capital forecast. The 
11 
adjustment was made to update the capital and cost of removal forecasts for 
12 
certain projects presented in Exhibit ___ (GIOP-1CU) for direct capital 
13 
expenditures and Exhibit ___ (GIOP-6CU) for indirect capital expenditures.  
14 
The corrections and update testimony of the GIOP discusses the specific 
15 
adjustments in more detail. 
16 
 
17 
The third adjustment updates the gas plant forecast to incorporate revised in-
18 
service dates for certain gas and facility projects, as discussed by the GIOP.

--- Page 22 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 20 of 24 
 
 
B. 
Deferred Taxes 
1 
Q. 
Please describe the changes made to the deferred tax forecasts, as shown 
2 
in Exhibit ___ (RRP-7CU), Schedule 3. 
3 
A. 
The Company made changes to rate base ADIT to (i) flow through the impact 
4 
of the return of excess ADIT, (ii) add the impact of taking bonus depreciation 
5 
on the fiscal year end March 31, 2019 federal income tax return, (iii) update 
6 
ADIT balances from December 2018 to March 2019, and (iv) flow through 
7 
the rate base ADIT impact of changes to book plant additions, cost of 
8 
removal, and book depreciation. 
9 
 
10 
Q. 
How does the change in excess ADIT amortization change rate base? 
11 
A. 
As the Company returns excess ADIT, excess ADIT regulatory liability that is 
12 
included in rate base decreases and rate base is correspondingly increased.  
13 
Rate base ADIT adjustments were made to reflect the updated amortization 
14 
amounts that flow through cost of service.  Also, the Company determined 
15 
that in the April 30 filing, the rate base adjustment included the excess ADIT 
16 
related to both National Grid USA Service Company and KEDLI.  
17 
Accordingly, the Company updated the rate base formula to include only the 
18 
amortization related to KEDLI. 
19 
 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 23 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 21 of 24 
 
Q. 
How did bonus depreciation change rate base ADIT?  
1 
A. 
After additional analysis and conversations with industry experts and other 
2 
industry peers, the Company determined it would deduct additional bonus 
3 
depreciation, in accordance with the pre-tax reform regulations.  Bonus 
4 
depreciation will be 40 percent for those assets started before September 28, 
5 
2017 and placed in service between April 1, 2018 and December 31, 2018.  
6 
Bonus depreciation of 30 percent will be taken on assets started before 
7 
September 28, 2017 and placed in service between January 1 and March 31, 
8 
2019.  As the consolidated National Grid group is in a net operating loss 
9 
(“NOL”) utilization position for the fiscal year, additional bonus depreciation 
10 
deductions will result in a reduction of the NOL utilization that is also 
11 
reflected in KEDLI’s rate base changes. 
12 
 
13

VIII. Regulatory Assets and Liabilities 
6 
Q. 
Please describe the corrections and updates shown in Schedule 2 of 
7 
Exhibit ___ (RRP-7CU). 
 
8 
A. 
The Company made three adjustments to the forecast regulatory asset and 
9 
liability balances at March 31, 2020.   
10 
 
11 
The forecast regulatory asset balance associated with SIR carrying charges 
12 
was reduced by approximately $2.4 million resulting from a correction to the 
13 
carrying charge calculation.  The original calculation did not properly reflect 
14 
the reduction to the total SIR deferred balance subject to carrying charges 
15 
resulting from a $40.5 million insurance recovery. 
16 
 
17 
Additionally, the forecast net Pension and OPEB deferred liability balance 
18 
was increased by approximately $1.4 million to reflect the changes resulting 
19 
from the updated actuarial forecast (discussed above). 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 25 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 23 of 24 
 
Lastly, the forecast net regulatory liability associated with the Capital Tracker 
1 
deferral and its associated carrying charges was increased by $0.017 million to 
2 
reflect the impact of the change in the capital forecast (also discussed above).    
3 
 
4 
Q. 
Do the changes in regulatory assets and liabilities have any impact on the 
5 
revenue requirement? 
6 
A. 
No.  All the adjusted regulatory assets and liability balances are excluded 
7 
from rate base and therefore have no effect on the revenue requirement.

Response: 
 
1.
a.
The Historic Test Year reflects costs of $0.071 million for KEDNY and $0.043 
million for KEDLI related to the management and operations audit in Case 18-M-
0195 (“Management Audit”).   
b. No adjustment was made to reflect Rate Year costs for the Management Audit.  As 
such, the costs embedded in the Rate Year are equivalent to the Historic Test Year 
costs plus general inflation.   
In preparing this response, the Company realized the above costs should be 
normalized and replaced with KEDNY and KEDLI’s allocable share of the $1.988 
million compensation limit set forth in the audit contract in the Management Audit.  
In corrections and updates, KEDNY and KEDLI will remove the amount included in 
the Historic Test Year and replace with the amortized portion of KEDNY and 
KEDLI’s allocable share of the Management Audit contract costs.     
2.
a-d. There are no costs or savings associated with implementation of recommendations in 
Case 13-G-0009 (Gas Management Audit), Case 13-M-0314 (“Data Audit”), or Case 
13-M-0449 (“Staffing Audit”) in the Historic Test Year or Rate Year, as the 
recommendations were implemented prior to the Historic Test Year and/or did not 
involve any incremental costs.  Benefits were qualitative in nature with no savings 
identified in the Rate Year.  
e.  The Management Audit is ongoing with a final report scheduled for September 
2019.  As such, any potential costs or savings are unknown at the moment.

accounting treatment of these work activities between National Grid’s New York gas 
distribution companies. As discussed in the testimony of the Revenue Requirements

costs, was made to the general contractors exhibit, Exhibit RRP-3, Schedule 2.  For the 
Company’s Corrections & Updates filing, the paving component will be broken out from

Based on discussions with Department of Public Service Staff, the Company is providing the

10.

11.
The adjustment to Remove Leak Repair Cost associated with the incremental leak repairs
completed to achieve the incentive for lowering the Type 3 backlog of leaks is not
directly related to specific line items on the Contractors workpaper.  Rather, the
adjustment removes a set amount of leak repair cost calculated by taking the number of
incremental leak repairs associated with reducing the Type 3 leak backlog (205 leak
repairs in calendar year 2018) multiplied by the average unit cost of a leak repair
($4,596).
Attachments 1 and 2 also include Contractor and Paving expense adjustments made to
normalize costs related to the capitalization policy change.  Note that the normalization
adjustment related to main replacement in the Company’s original filing, and presented
on Attachment 1, was $0.004 million.  This amount was related to capital work orders
and not expense work orders and, therefore, should not have been part of the
normalization adjustment because it was not in expense.  For the same reason, a similar
revision is presented on Attachment 2.  The normalization adjustment related to main
replacement included in the Company’s original filing, as presented on Attachment 2, is
$0.029 million.  This amount will be reduced to $0.003 million.  These revisions, as
shown on Attachment 1 and Attachment 2, will be reflected in the Company’s
Corrections & Updates filing.

SUBJECT:
Other Expenses (FL Accrual)- KEDNY 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
Referring to the MS Excel File, “Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to Exhibit___(RRP-3), 
Schedule 7, WP 1,” explain what each CO Documents type of FL Accrual item listed below is 
and explain why KEDNY includes these amounts in other expenses. 
1.
159414175 of $12.55 million; 
2.
WAN Invoice Allocations of $0.92 million; 
3.
Appreciate Award Dec FY19 of $0.49 million; and 
4.
Accrue Travel Expense of $0.04 million. 
Response: 
 
1.
The purpose of this entry is to post an accrual related to City State Construction charges 
included in the deferred expense account that are in excess of the amounts billable under 
existing reimbursement agreements.  Charges to the deferred expense account for 
disconnect/reconnect and watch guard work are billed to the City at an agreed upon rate 
and amounts above that are posted to expense.  This accrual is an estimate of the amounts 
that should be posted to expense based on what has historically been invoiced.  The 
accrual represents charges for active projects that will be billed at the completion of the 
project.  
Exhibit____(RRP-3CU)
Schedule 7
Workpaper 4
Page 1 of 4


--- Page 414 ---
Form 103 
2.
This amount represents the December 2018 accrual for network service and telecom 
vendors that have provided services for the month that have not been billed.  The accruals 
are booked to other expense and reversed the following month. 
3.
This entry was to record the December 2018 accrual for the unbilled appreciate program 
costs.  In addition, other expense in the historic test year includes the reversal of the prior 
year’s accruals, resulting in a net amount related to appreciate program costs in other 
expense of $0.07 million.   
As described in the testimony of the Revenue Requirement Panel and shown on 
Exhibit__(RRP-3), Schedule 1, Workpaper 3, the Company removed from the Historic 
Test Year the vendor costs associated with the appreciate program.  The Company 
inadvertently excluded the historic test year net accrual amount in other expense from the 
adjustment.  The Company will remove the $0.07 million in its Corrections and Updates 
filing.  KEDLI will also remove the $(.01) million from its other expense in Corrections 
and Updates filing.   
4.
The purpose of this entry is to accrue travel card transactions that have not posted to the 
books as of December 2018.  The accrual is booked to other expense and reversed the 
following month.  The actuals will subsequently be posted to the actual lines of 
accounting.

Gas Utilities Rates 
Request for Information 
FROM: 
DPS Staff, Hina M. Thalho 
TO: 
National Grid, Revenue Requirements Panel 
SUBJECT:
Other Expenses - KEDLI 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
Referring to the MS Excel file, “Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to Exhibit___(RRP-3), 
Schedule 7, WP 1,” identify and explain each cost element within each activity listed below. 
1. Expense of $(0.52) million; and 
2. Various of $ (5.36) million. 
Response: 
 
1. The credit amount of $(0.52) million is the remaining LIPA funds that remain in 
KEDLI’s cash subledger.  All debts owed to LIPA had been applied to monies 
received from LIPA and the remaining balance was recorded as other expense.  As 
this was related to a prior period and will not recur in the Rate Year, the amount 
should have been normalized from the Historic Test Year.  The Company will reflect 
this adjustment in its Corrections and Updates filing. 
2. The amount in the “various” activity represents a topside entry related to the reclass 
of Administrative and General (“A&G”) costs.  A&G costs were initially expensed to 
FERC accounts 920/921, but as part of the A&G Overhead Study, it was determined 
that portions of the expensed costs should have been capitalized.  This represents the  
Exhibit____(RRP-3CU)
Schedule 7
Workpaper 4
Page 3 of 4


--- Page 416 ---
Form 103 
CY18 amount that should have reduced O&M expense.  As this was a topside entry, 
it was not recorded to a specific activity and therefore was classified as “various” for 
Workpaper 1.

Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1. 
For the IT/OT Discovery and Implementation program in the Rate Year, provide the 
approved sanction paper or approval document that describes the program or project, 
project justifications, cost breakdown, security benefits, and alternative solutions. 
2. 
Provide in MS Excel file format, progress made in the IT/OT Discovery and 
Implementation program versus the projected schedule in the three previous calendar 
years 2016-2018, and to date 2019. Include a detailed explanation for any delays or 
unscheduled interruptions to the program. 
3. 
Provide in MS Excel file format, the actual capital expenditures versus the approved 
capital expenditures budget for the IT/OT Discovery and Implementation program for the 
previous three calendar years 2016-2018, and to-date 2019.   
Response: 
 
1.
Please see Attachment 1 for the sanction paper that was also provided in the response to 
DPS-487 at Attachment 4, page 107. Please note that the IT/OT Discovery & 
Implementation program has been renamed as the High Value Asset Discovery & 
Implementation project.   
2.
The project commenced in November 2018 and the project schedule is included in 
Section 1.14 (Key Milestones) of the sanction paper.  The Company maintains a Portfolio 
tracking report but there is no separate spreadsheet in MS Excel File Format that tracks

project schedule information on an individual project basis.  The information is also 
tracked and maintained within the Microsoft Project On-Line Tool.   
The High Value Asset Discovery & Implementation was initially delayed due to a review 
of the Cyber Security strategy in 2018 and is currently paused as the new Chief 
Information Security Officer is reviewing the prioritization and timing of several 
initiatives.   
In addition, the Company discovered that an incorrect project in-service date for the 
project was included in Exhibit_(ITP-4).  This will be corrected in the Company’s 
Corrections and Update Filing. 
3.
The project was budgeted for as part of the Digital Risk and Security (DR&S) Future 
Program in the FY19 Information Technology (IT) Investment Plan and as a separate 
standalone project (High Value Asset Discovery & Implementation) in the FY20 IT Plan. 
Please see Attachment 40 in the response to DPS-487 for a copy of the financial work 
book that contains up-to-date budget, actual, and project forecast information.  Shown 
below is an excerpt of the budget and actuals for the project for FY19 and FY20.  
Lastly, please note that the financials are reported on a fiscal year basis as this is the 
Company’s standard practice for tracking and reporting on project financials.

SUBJECT:
Labor - Capitalization 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1.
On an on-going, monthly basis, provide an updated 12-month average of KEDLI’s actual
labor costs, broken down between expense, capital, and other, beginning January 2019.
2.
As stated on p.62, ln 3 of KEDLI’s Revenue Requirement Panel testimony “[t]he
Company forecast 57.62 percent of total labor costs would be capitalized in the Rate Year
(RY). The forecast is based on the Historic Test Year (HTY) percentage of labor costs
capitalized.”
a.
Does KEDLI anticipate a greater level of capital work to be performed during the
RY? If yes, explain why the Company believes the amount of labor costs
capitalized in the HTY, is indicative of the amount of labor costs to be capitalized
in the RY.
b.
For KEDLI, provide the dollar amount of capital work performed during the
HTY.
c.
For KEDLI, provide the dollar amount of capital work to be performed during the
RY.
d.
For KEDLI, provide the dollar amount of capital work performed for Calendar
Years (CY) 2016 and 2017.
e.
For KEDLI, provide the percent of total labor costs capitalized for CY 2016 and
2017.
3.
As stated on p.61, ln 9 of KEDLI’s Revenue Requirements Panel testimony “[w]ith
respect to KEDLI, the Company made adjustments to: (i) reflect changes to the
capitalization policy to remove the 50-foot threshold and capitalize all main installation
activities…” Explain whether KEDLI accounted for this change when determining the
Exhibit______(RRP-11CU)

Schedule 23
Workpaper 15

--- Page 643 ---
Form 103 
HTY percentage of labor costs capitalized. If yes, provide the supporting calculation. If 
not, explain why not, and provide an updated calculation including this change. 
Response: 
 
1. 
Please see Attachment 1 for the rolling 12-month average of KEDLI’s originating 
company labor costs, broken down between operating expense, non-operating expense, 
capital expense and other, beginning January 2019. 
2a. 
Yes, the Company anticipates a greater level of capital work to be performed during the  
Rate Year.  However, an increase in capital work does not warrant an adjustment to the 
Rate Year labor capitalization rate.  The Company’s labor expense forecast follows 
Historic Test Year (“HTY”) accounting.  Specifically, the labor model applies the HTY 
capitalization ratio to a total labor amount that is calculated based on headcount at the 
end of the HTY.  The Company’s level of O&M expense work in the HTY will not 
decrease in the Rate Year because of more capital work.  Indeed, the same base level of 
O&M expense work is projected to continue in the Rate Year.  Therefore, applying an 
HTY capitalization ratio is appropriate.   
With respect to the projected increase in capital work, that work will be supported 
through the addition of the proposed FTEs set forth in Exhibit ___ (RRP-3), Schedule 27 
(Other Initiatives).  These incremental FTEs receive an 85 to 90 percent allocation to 
capital labor.     
Importantly, use of the HTY capitalization rate to forecast Rate Year labor expense has 
been used to set rates in National Grid’s most recent rate case proceedings (see Cases 16-
G-0058 and 16-G-0059 and Cases 17-E-0238 and 17-G-0239).  If the labor capitalization 
rate were adjusted, an adjustment would need to be made to increase contractor expense 
to cover the O&M expense work performed in the HTY that will continue in the Rate 
Year.   
2b. 
Please see Exhibit ___ (RRP-3), Schedule 23, Page 9 for the amount of capital labor 
charged to KEDLI during the Historic Test Year.  Please see Exhibit ___ (GIOP-1) for the 
total gas direct capital work in the Historic Test Year. 
2c. 
 Please see Exhibit ___ (RRP-3), Schedule 23, Page 9 for the amount of capital labor 
charged to KEDLI during the Rate Year.  Please see Exhibits ___ (GIOP-1) and (GIOP-
7) for the total gas direct and indirect capital work in the Rate Year. 
2d. 
Please see the response to DPS-032 for capital labor charged to KEDLI for calendar years 
2016 and 2017.  Please see the response to DPS-084 for total capital work performed in 
fiscal years 2014 through 2018. 
2e.  
Please see Attachment 2 for the total capitalization rate for calendar years 2016 and 2017.  
The rate shown on Attachment 2 was calculated using the same components of total 
Exhibit______(RRP-11CU)
Workpapers to Exhibit (RRP-3CU) 
Schedule 23
Workpaper 15
Page 2 of 5


--- Page 644 ---
Form 103 
originating KEDLI labor as those used to calculate the referenced 57.62% capitalization 
rate. 
3. 
Yes, the Company accounted for this change when determining the HTY percentage of 
labor costs capitalized.  Please refer to Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to Exhibit 
RRP-3, Schedule 23, Workpaper 10 for the KEDLI HTY adjustment to reflect the change 
to the capitalization policy to remove the 50-foot threshold and capitalize all main 
installation activities.   
KEDLI’s adjustment to the HTY was a reduction of $119,726 to KEDLI’s originating 
company labor expense and an increase to capital labor.  In reviewing the adjustment, it 
was determined that the adjustment should have been $116,684 to KEDLI originating 
company labor costs and $3,042 to Service Company originating company labor costs.  
The Company will include this adjustment in its Corrections & Updates filing.

1. 
Please see the Company’s response to DPS-029 for the latest KEDNY TWU Local 101 
and IBEW Local 3 union contracts supporting the associated wage increases used in the 
Rate Year labor forecast. 
2. 
The KEDNY TWU Local 101 contract expires on October 15, 2019   and given the 
timing, it was reasonable to assume that the new bargained contract would, at a 
minimum, include a 1.5% wage increase for October 2019 as the terms of the recently 
expired contract included wage increases of 1.5% each April and October of 1.5%.  
Therefore, the Company included an assumption of a 1.5% wage increase for October 
2019 in its Rate Year labor forecast.   
Notwithstanding the foregoing, on April 27, 2019 National Grid and TWU Local 101 
negotiated a new three-year contract.  The contract term, which commences on October 
16, 2019 and ends on October 15, 2022, includes a wage increase of 2.75% effective 
October 16, 2019, a 3.0% wage increase effective on October 16, 2020 and a 3.0% wage 
increase effective on October 16, 2021.  Please see Attachment 1 for the latest 
memorandum of agreement between National Grid and TWU Local 101 dated April 27, 
2019.    The increases resulting from this memorandum will be included in the 
Company’s Corrections and Updates filing.

Gas Utilities Rates 
Request for Information 
FROM: 
DPS Staff, John Castano 
TO: 
National Grid, Gas Infrastructure and Operations Panel (GIOP) 
SUBJECT:
Capitalization Policy Change 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1.
As stated on p. 87 of KEDLI’s Gas Infrastructure and Operations Panel testimony, “[t]he 
Company is proposing to remove the 50-foot threshold and capitalize all main installation 
activities in accordance with the FERC Chart of Accounts –Gas – Operating Expense 
Instructions, Accounts Mains and 376 Mains. This change will standardize the 
accounting treatment of these work activities between National Grid’s New York gas 
distribution companies. As discussed in the testimony of the Revenue Requirements 
Panel, the Company has normalized its Historic Test Year to reflect the change from 
expense to capital for distribution and transmission main installation, and the Company’s 
capital investment forecasts also reflect this capitalization change. 
a.
For KEDLI, identify all cost elements in which a normalizing adjustment was 
made to account for the capitalization of installments of main under 50-feet. 
b.
For KEDLI, identify the cost elements in which a normalizing adjustment was not 
made for the capitalization of installments of main under 50-feet, and explain why 
this normalizing adjustment was not warranted. 
Response: 
 
a.
For KEDLI, all cost elements containing expenses in the HTY associated with 50 
feet or less of main installation were normalized to reflect the Rate Year and Data 
Years’ change in capitalization policy described in the Gas Infrastructure and 
Exhibit______(RRP-11CU)
Workpapers to Exhibit RRP-3CU 
Schedule 23
Workpaper 3
Page 1 of 2


--- Page 652 ---
Form 103 
Operations Panel testimony at pages 97 and 98, with the exception of the 
transportation cost element discussed in Part (b) below.  
Because the Rate Year and Data Years’ expense in the following cost elements is 
forecast by inflating the normalized HTY expense amount, these cost elements 
have discrete HTY normalization adjustments applied directly in the exhibit 
removing the amount of HTY expense related to the 50 feet or less of main 
installation: 
i. RRP-3, Schedule 2: Contractors 
ii. RRP-3, Schedule 7: Other 
iii. RRP-3, Schedule 23: Labor 
The cost elements listed below do not have discrete normalization adjustments 
applied because the Rate Year forecast is not based on HTY expense inflated.  
Instead, the Rate Year and Data Years’ amounts are forecast in total and the 
expense amount determined by applying the labor capitalization rate.  Because 
labor has been normalized for the capitalization policy change (as shown in the 
cost elements list above), the labor capitalization rate based on that labor has been 
normalized.  By applying that labor capitalization rate to the total forecast cost for 
the cost elements below, the resulting expense amount is normalized for the 
capitalization policy change. 
iv. RRP-3, Schedule 11: FAS 106 – OPEB  
v. RRP-3, Schedule 12: FAS 112 
vi. RRP-3, Schedule 13: Healthcare 
vii. RRP-3, Schedule 14: Group Life Insurance 
viii. RRP-3, Schedule 16: Pensions 
ix. RRP-3, Schedule 17: Thrift Plan 
x. RRP-3, Schedule 18: Worker’s Comp 
xi. RRP-3, Schedule 23: Labor (Variable Pay) 
b.
The one cost element that was inadvertently not normalized for the capitalization 
policy change is transportation expense.  The capital and expense ratios of total 
transportation costs in the HTY are applied to the Rate Year and Data Years’ 
forecast of total transportation costs to obtain the expense portion.  Because the 
HTY capital and expense ratios for transportation costs were not normalized for 
the capitalization policy change, the Rate Year and Data Years’ transportation 
expense has not been normalized.  HTY transportation expense associated with 
the 50 feet or less of main installation is $.038 million for KEDLI.  The Company 
will make this adjustment in its Corrections & Updates filing.
